name: judy
content: Long-form stress case follows. The inbox content column is a flex column, so the interesting question is not whether text wraps but whether the wrap point is computed from the display width of the content column rather than from the remaining bytes in the row. A row is TIME(12) plus a separator, CHANNEL(12) plus a separator, THREAD(16) plus a separator, and NAME(12) plus a separator, which means the content column starts somewhere past column fifty on a one-hundred-column terminal. Drop the NAME column and it starts past column thirty-eight. Drop CHANNEL as well and it starts past column twenty-six. Each of those starting points has to be recomputed whenever a column is dropped, and each of them has to be recomputed against the display width of the name rather than the byte length of the name, because a name made of double-width runes occupies twice the columns it occupies in bytes. So this message is long enough that it will wrap several times under every one of those budgets, which is the point: if the wrap looks right at one terminal width and wrong at another, the column math is being done once and cached, or is being done in bytes somewhere, or the separator width is being counted twice on one branch and not the other. Read the rendering, not this sentence.

name: ivan
content: Column dropping order should be NAME, then CHANNEL, then THREAD, then TIME, and replies stay aligned to the CONTENT column at every width.
